assumptions.basis: Depth tier requested by the caller; it sets the paper budget for the round. null means the caller did not state one.
Hard ceiling on papers read this round. Every coverage count is bounded by it, so an absent relationship may be a budget artefact.
Hard ceiling on distinct corpus queries issued this round.
Publication window the search was restricted to. null means no window was requested, NOT that the corpus is complete.
Fixed weights in score_link. Chosen, not fitted: no labelled corpus exists to fit them against.
Study-design quality prior. An out-of-vocabulary study_type scores as `unknown` (0.4) rather than silently matching something close.
Multiplier applied to a preprint's design score, for absence of peer review.

Only a paper's own results count toward a link's STATE, its agreement term and its independence term -- a review restating forty studies is one paper, and is not independent evidence for any of them. Note the exception: `evidence_quality` averages over every finding on the link, cited background included.
Constants in the open-triangle gap ranking, including the 0.6 ceiling that keeps a gap a proposal rather than a finding.

headline.plain_language: Read 2 papers and mapped 37 relationships from 44 quote-backed findings; 1 are corroborated by more than one paper, 28 rest on a single paper, and 1 are disputed.
headline.title: Evidence graph: 37 relationships from 20 papers

limitations.message: 1 retained findings carry a quote that was checked against source text and did NOT appear in it. This is not a wording difference -- the match is whitespace- and typography-normalized -- so treat these as unsourced: f26.

8 of 44 retained findings carry a quote that was never checked against source text, because no source text was supplied for their paper. Their quotes are shown but must not be treated as verified, and their evidence grade is capped at LOW.
stop_reason=no_new_results. Only `complete` means the literature was exhausted rather than the budget.
6 intervention nodes have no molecular target in the graph.
The round did not record the search queries it issued, so the search cannot be reproduced or audited from this output.
28 of 37 relationships rest on exactly one paper.
The search was truncated (stop_reason=no_new_results). Absence of a relationship is evidence about what was read, not about what exists.
These metrics are structural counts of the graph itself and reference neither evidence nor an assumption: metric.entities.
1 relationships have primary papers reporting opposite directions; `why` names the differing conditions where they could be identified.
link.confidence.overall is a heuristic score (0.4*agreement + 0.4*evidence_quality + 0.2*independence), not a probability. Do not threshold it as one.

No source-text hash for 3 of 20 papers, and no Paperclip document id or page/figure locator is recorded for any paper -- the corpus does not expose stable document ids through the search interface used here. Evidence locators fall back to the finding's section label.
1 values in this block are null because they were never recorded or could not be computed. Null is not zero and not false. Full list: assumption.years.
No publication window was requested, so a windowed absence cannot be distinguished from a real one.

lineage.transformation: Kept only when the quote matches the paper's source text verbatim after NFKC and whitespace folding; deduplicated by (paper, relationship, folded quote) so a retried round cannot double-count.
SHA-256 of the exact source text the quotes were checked against. null when none was supplied.
Merged on UniProt accession first, then on normalized name; a conflicting accession blocks a name merge.
Bound to the (from, how, to) triple the round it first appears and carried forward through entity merges, so delta and changed_in_round keep naming the same relationship across rounds.
Counts of yes/no/no_effect over own-result findings only.
Emitted only for a disagreed link whose supporting and contradicting findings report non-overlapping conditions.
Open triangles ranked multiplicatively; ids keyed on the missing pair so test_gap can target one by id across rounds.
Diff against the stored prior round. Derived, never stored.

metrics.meaning: How many matched papers were actually opened this round.

metrics.label: Papers contributing evidence
metrics.meaning: Papers that produced at least one quote-backed finding. The gap between read and used is the screening loss.

metrics.label: Quote-verified findings
metrics.meaning: Findings whose quote was matched verbatim against the paper's source text. This is a string match, not a judgement.

metrics.label: Findings with unchecked quotes
metrics.meaning: Findings kept without source text to check their quote against. Never counted as verified.

metrics.label: Findings whose quote did not match
metrics.meaning: Findings whose quote was checked against source text and was not found in it. Treat as unsourced.

metrics.label: Relationships
metrics.meaning: Distinct (subject, predicate, object) triples supported by at least one paper's own result.

metrics.label: Disputed relationships
metrics.meaning: Relationships where primary papers report opposite directions. These are the ones worth reading by hand.

metrics.label: Corroborated relationships
metrics.meaning: Relationships where two or more papers agree on direction.

metrics.label: Single-source relationships
metrics.meaning: Relationships resting on exactly one paper. Uncorroborated, not wrong.

metrics.label: Reported-null relationships
metrics.meaning: Relationships where the only primary evidence is an explicit no-effect result. Kept separately so a null is never read as an absence of evidence.

metrics.label: Untested relationships proposed
metrics.meaning: Pairs connected through an intermediate but with no direct link reported. Proposals for the next round, not findings.

metrics.label: Mean heuristic confidence
metrics.meaning: Mean of the per-relationship heuristic score. A ranking aid, NOT a probability that any relationship is true.

metrics.label: Distinct entities
metrics.meaning: Nodes after accession-first merging of synonyms.

steps.label: Search the corpus
steps.method: Paperclip full-text search over the biomedical corpus

steps.label: Read and screen
steps.method: Full-text read, then keep papers that yield a quote-backed finding

steps.formula: fold(NFKC(quote)) is a substring of fold(NFKC(source_text)); non-matching findings are discarded, findings with no source text are retained and marked quote_verified=null
steps.label: Verify every quote against source text
steps.method: Mechanical substring match, not a model judgement

steps.formula: a conflicting accession BLOCKS a name merge, so human Q9NWZ3 and mouse Q8R4K2 stay distinct
steps.label: Merge synonymous entities
steps.method: UniProt accession first, then separator-insensitive normalized name

steps.formula: state = disagreed if yes and no; agreed if >=2 one way; single_source if exactly one; no_effect if only explicit nulls
steps.label: Group findings into relationships
steps.method: Group by (from, how, to) over own-result findings only

steps.formula: 0.5 + (yes - no) / (2 * (yes + no)); a lone source is 0.5, never 1.0
steps.label: Agreement term
steps.method: Direction balance across a relationship's own results

steps.label: Evidence-quality term
steps.method: Study-design prior, averaged over the relationship's findings

steps.formula: (distinct first authors - 1) / (papers - 1); one group is not a consensus, so a single group scores 0.0
steps.label: Independence term
steps.method: Distinct first authors behind a relationship

steps.label: Combine into a heuristic confidence score
steps.method: Fixed-weight linear combination. HEURISTIC -- not a probability, not calibrated against any outcome

steps.formula: min(conf_AB, conf_BC) * basis_AB * basis_BC * independence * (1/sqrt(gaps spawned by the hub)) * (1 + 0.12*log2(routes)), capped at 0.6
steps.label: Rank untested relationships
steps.method: Open triangles (A-B and B-C exist, A-C does not), ranked multiplicatively to break the ties a min() score produces

limitations: low/central/high are the observed minimum, mean and maximum of the per-relationship heuristic score across the 37 relationships in this graph. They are an observed range -- NOT percentiles, NOT a confidence interval, and NOT a sampling distribution.
The score is a ranking aid over what was read. It is not a probability that a relationship is true, and it is not calibrated against any outcome.
seed and draws are null because assembly is deterministic: the same round bundle produces byte-identical output.
The dominant uncertainty is not in the score, it is in coverage: 7 of 71 matched papers were read this round.
uncertainty.method: Heuristic confidence decomposition (agreement, evidence quality, independence). No sampling, no model fitting and no statistical inference is performed.
